extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners on making and formulating rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101, 112, 103(b), and related statutory/regulatory provisions (including Atomic Energy Act procedures), with required form paragraphs and explanatory detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103(b) requirements for biotechnological processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a timely election by the applicant for patent to proceed under this subsection, a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition of matter that is novel under section 102 and nonobvious under subsection (a) of this section shall be considered nonobvious if-(A) claims to the process and the composition of matter are contained in either the same application for patent or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; and (B) the composition of matter, and the process at the time it was invented, were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 103(b) is applicable to biotechnological processes only and precludes rejection of process claims which involve the use or making of certain nonobvious biotechnological compositions under 35 U.S.C. 103(a). The petition under 37 CFR 1.182 must establish that all requirements of 35 U.S.C. 103(b) have been satisfied. An election is timely if made no later than the earlier of payment of the issue fee or filing of an appeal brief in an application that contains a composition claim not rejected under 102 or 103. For certain applications pending on or after Nov. 1, 1995 with issue fee paid prior to Mar. 26, 1996, timeliness may be satisfied per 37 CFR 1.312(b). If granted in error without election, reissue may permit consideration of process claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process/composition claim linkage and co-expiration under 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent issued on a process under paragraph (1) shall also contain the claims to the composition of matter used in or made by that process, or shall, if such composition of matter is claimed in another patent, be set to expire on the same date as such other patent, notwithstanding section 154.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must ensure either the process patent contains composition claims or, if composition claimed in another patent, patents must expire on same date; this requirement is part of petition showing under 103(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biotechnological process' for 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (1), the term 'biotechnological process' means-(A) a process of genetically altering or otherwise inducing a single- or multi-celled organism to-(i) express an exogenous nucleotide sequence, (ii) inhibit, eliminate, augment, or alter expression of an endogenous nucleotide sequence, or (iii) express a specific physiological characteristic not naturally associated with said organism; (B) cell fusion procedures yielding a cell line that expresses a specific protein, such as a monoclonal antibody; and (C) a method of using a product produced by a process defined by subparagraph (A) or (B), or a combination of subparagraphs (A) and (B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 303(b) applies only to processes falling within this statutory definition; examiner should confirm the process falls within these categories when considering 103(b) treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination priority: focus on prior art rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary object of the examination of an application is to determine whether or not the claims are patentable over the prior art. This consideration should not be relegated to a secondary position while undue emphasis is given to nonprior art or 'technical' rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate effort on truly essential matters; minimize or eliminate effort on technical rejections which are not really critical. Where a major technical rejection is proper (e.g., lack of proper disclosure, undue breadth, utility, etc.) such rejection should be stated with a full development of the reasons rather than a mere conclusion with stereotyped expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to state rejections precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the language in the form paragraphs is incorporated in the Office action to state the rejection, there will be less chance of a misunderstanding as to the grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., ¶7.04, ¶7.05.x, ¶7.30.01, etc.) in first actions on the merits and final rejections as required; follow Examiner Notes about when paragraphs must precede others and how often they may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 101 prevents two patents issuing on the same invention to the same applicant; the 'same invention' means identical subject matter is being claimed. If more than one patent is sought, a statutory double patenting rejection applies for claims included in more than one application that are directed to the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 800 (specifically §804) for criteria relevant to double patenting. Use Form Paragraphs 8.30, 8.31, and 8.32 for statutory double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention must fall within one of the four categories of invention recited in 35 U.S.C. 101: process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter. Additionally, a claimed invention must not be directed to one of the judicially recognized exceptions (scientific truths, abstract principles, abstract intellectual concepts, laws of nature, natural phenomena, abstract ideas, mental processes, processes of human thinking, and systems that depend for their operation on human intelligence alone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2105 and §2106 for further guidance. If rejecting under 101, explain why the claimed invention, although nominally within a category, is directed to a judicial exception, and whether it would preempt all substantial practical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Energy Act limitation on patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Atomic Energy Act prohibits patents granted on any invention or discovery that is useful solely in the utilization of special nuclear material or atomic energy in an atomic weapon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications disclosing or appearing to disclose inventions related to atomic energy must be reported to the Department of Energy per 37 CFR 1.14(d). TC work group 3640 screens such applications and forwards related applications to Licensing and Review in TC work group 3640; see MPEP §706.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection on the ground of lack of utility is appropriate when (1) it is not apparent why the invention is 'useful' because applicant has failed to identify any specific and substantial utility and there is no well established utility, or (2) an assertion of specific and substantial utility for the invention is not credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base a utility rejection on the invention being frivolous, fraudulent or against public policy. For inoperativeness or lack of utility, consider rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 (enablement) and apply In re Wands factors for undue experimentation; see MPEP §§2107 and 2164.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.04 Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 101 (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.04: Quotation of 35 U.S.C. 101 must precede the first use of 35 U.S.C. 101 in all first actions on the merits and final rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must precede first use of 35 U.S.C. 101 in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Use paragraph 7.103 where the statute is not being re-cited in an action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.05.011 Rejection for method claims directed to abstract idea
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph should only be used when rejecting method claim(s) directed to an abstract idea: 'the claimed invention is not directed to patent eligible subject matter... claim(s) [1] is/are determined to be directed to an abstract idea. The rationale for this determination is explained below: [2]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the accompanying explanation, discuss relevant factors with respect to the claim as a whole and explain why the claim is interpreted to be an abstract idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.05.01 Rejection header requirements under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.05: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because ...' (heading only)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be followed by one or more specific form paragraphs (7.05.01, 7.05.011, 7.05.012, 7.05.013, 7.05.02, 7.05.03, or other). Explain the rejection following the statute recitation. Precede this header by ¶7.04 in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.05.012 Dependent claim rejection when additional limitations insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claim(s) when analyzed as a whole are held to be patent ineligible under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the additional recited limitation(s) fail(s) to establish that the claim(s) is/are not directed to an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the additional limitations are no more than a field of use or merely involve insignificant extra-solution activity (e.g., data gathering). The explanation must be sufficient to establish a prima facie case of patent ineligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.05.013 Rejection for law of nature / natural principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when method claim(s) have a law of nature/natural principle as a claim limitation: 'claim(s) [1] is/are determined to be directed to a law of nature/natural principle. The rationale... is explained below: [2]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the natural principle limiting the claim and explain why additional elements/steps do not integrate the natural principle into the method and/or why they are not sufficient to amount to significantly more (e.g., are extra-solution activity or purely conventional). Must establish a prima facie case of ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility-related rejections tied to 35 U.S.C. 112 (¶7.05.02, ¶7.05.03, formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims lacking specific and substantial asserted utility, lacking credible asserted utility, or being inoperative should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 and/or 112 as appropriate (¶7.05.02, ¶7.05.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where specification would not enable one skilled in the art, make a separate rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (enablement) using In re Wands factors. Use Formats A, B, or C as appropriate and provide bracketed explanations per the form paragraphs. Address multiple utilities individually (see ¶7.05.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.05.03 Inoperative rejection (lack of credible utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.05.03: 'the disclosed invention is inoperative and therefore lacks utility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the invention is inoperative and lacks credible asserted utility; insert claim numbers and specific explanatory text per the Format C instructions. Relate to enablement issues as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Energy Act reporting and TC 3640 screening procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received are screened by Technology Center (TC) work group 3640 personnel under 37 CFR 1.14(d) for inventions/discoveries relating to atomic energy; such reporting to DOE does not determine that the subject matter is useful or in categories specified by the Atomic Energy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers subsequently added must be inspected promptly by the examiner; if amended to relate to atomic energy, forward promptly to Licensing and Review in TC work group 3640. All rejections based upon sections 151(a), 152, and 155 of the Atomic Energy Act follow procedures in MPEP §706.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.30.01 Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph: 'The specification shall contain a written description of the invention, and of the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art... and shall set forth the best mode contemplated...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statute quotation is required in first actions on the merits and final rejections (use ¶7.103 where statute not re-cited). Form paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.30.02 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.31.01 Written description rejection criteria (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as failing the written description requirement when 'the claim(s) contains subject matter which was not described in the specification in such a way as to reasonably convey to one skilled in the art that the inventor(s) ... had possession of the claimed invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracketed explanation, identify by page/line and/or drawings the subject matter not properly described and explain the examiner’s position, including unresolved applicant responses that raise doubt as to possession. Must be preceded by ¶7.30.01 or ¶7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.31.02 Enablement rejection criteria (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as failing to comply with the enablement requirement where the specification does not enable one skilled in the art to make and/or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claimed subject matter not enabled and explain why not enabling, applying In re Wands factors and undue experimentation analysis. If problem is scope, consider ¶7.31.03. Precede by ¶7.30.01 or ¶7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.31.03 Scope of enablement: commensurability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the specification, while enabling for certain aspects, 'does not reasonably provide enablement for' other claim aspects; 'the specification does not enable any person skilled in the art to [make/use] the invention commensurate in scope with these claims.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify portions of the specification that are enabling and the specific claim aspects not enabled. Explain why the specification does not enable the claimed scope, applying In re Wands factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.31.04 Best mode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the best mode contemplated by the inventor has not been disclosed; 'Evidence of concealment of the best mode is based upon [2].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede by ¶7.30.01 or ¶7.103. In bracketed explanation, insert basis for holding that best mode has been concealed (e.g., quality of disclosure effectively results in concealment). Use of this form paragraph should be rare; see MPEP §§2165-2165.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.33.01 Essential subject matter missing from claims (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected where a feature considered critical or essential by applicant to the practice of the claimed invention is missing from the claim and the disclosure is not enabling for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite the omitted subject matter, give rationale for considering it essential, and cite statements/arguments/drawings showing the feature was considered essential by the applicant. Precede by ¶7.30.01 or ¶7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.30.02 / ¶7.34.01 Indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention; 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by ¶7.30.02 or ¶7.103. Identify particular terms or limitations rendering the claim indefinite and explain why; follow MPEP §§2171-2174. Use ¶7.34.02 - ¶7.34.11 as applicable for more specific indefiniteness reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.02 Inconsistent terminology / applicant-as-lexicographer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant acts as his or her own lexicographer to specifically define a term contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the claim term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the term usage in the claim, the meaning assigned by applicant, and the accepted meaning with supporting citation (textbook/dictionary). Precede by ¶7.34.01; use only where specification does not clearly redefine the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.03 Relative term/term of degree rendering claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term or term of degree (e.g., 'about', 'substantial') renders the claim indefinite if not defined by the claim and the specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which parameter or limitation is rendered indefinite and why one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of scope. Precede by ¶7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.04 Broad range and narrow range in same claim (indefiniteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range in the same claim is considered indefinite because the resulting claim does not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the patent protection desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the broader range and the narrower range and their locations in the claim. Precede by ¶7.34.01. May be modified to other indefiniteness instances where broad language is followed by 'such as' and then narrow language.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.05 Lack of antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim recites a limitation without sufficient antecedent basis (e.g., 'said lever' without earlier 'a lever'), making scope indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes claim scope indeterminate. Precede by ¶7.34.01. Identify the limitation and where it appears in the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.06 Use claims that recite use without steps (indefinite/improper process claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim providing for the use of something but not setting forth any steps delimiting how this use is actually practiced is indefinite and may be an improper process claim under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that reciting a use without active positive steps fails to define a process. Cite examples and precedents (e.g., Ex parte Dunki, Clinical Products v. Brenner). Precede by ¶7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.34.11 'Means' modifier lacking specified function (means-plus-function issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the modifier of 'means' does not specify a function, it is impossible to determine equivalents as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, rendering the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert what is being used and demonstrate absence of a specified function. Cite relevant MPEP section (2173.05(q)) and precede by ¶7.34.01.
